metrics.action: Write a test for a {gap} requirement, or for one carrying no test and no annotation, then record its break with `./le rfc record`: a requirement counts as proven only when a discrimination record still verifies on a walked summary. Not-applicable needs no test.
metrics.detail: 44.0% of the 4753 gated MUSTs of the walked RFCs ze implements are proven by a recorded break: a discrimination record that still verifies against this tree. 0 of the 194 RFCs ze implements are not walked yet: their requirement lists are unbounded, so they are left out of both counts rather than measured. The gate holds a wider set -- 4787 gated MUSTs across 203 enrolled RFCs -- and of the 2340 of those not proven in both polarities: 46 not-applicable (recorded as not binding ze; the owner ruling of 2026-08-31 presumes most of these need re-homing, so they stay inside the denominator above rather than being subtracted from it), 1515 known gap (unimplemented, genuinely untested), 19 partial (scoped evidence with a remaining gap; subset of annotated, zero whole-requirement credit), 487 single-polarity -- those DO have a passing tagged test, just one side of the pair, and the RFC gate fails if that test is missing -- 239 met by a layer under ze on state ze installs, which the annotation names with the producer that installs it: those are MET and are not proven by ze, so they count in the denominator above and never in the share, 34 conditional on an optional feature ze does not offer, each quoting the RFC sentence that makes it optional: the condition is false, so nothing is owed, 0 blocked by a verified Linux kernel limitation: the obligation still binds and remains unmet, with no proof credit and no denominator reduction, and 0 with no test and no annotation at all, which is what `./le rfc check` is red about. Gaps, remaining partial obligations and unexcused rows are work Ze owes; Linux limits separately name the primitive the kernel cannot provide. Apart from every figure above, 14 rows carry {rollup}: each derives its state from rows already counted here, and none is in the denominator.
